units.known_address_notes: Zokyo 2023-06-07 report scopes the TruFin 'Staker' contract (repo github.com/TruFin-io/staker-audit @71e300d3, MATIC staking vault with totalShares/sharePrice). DefiLlama's TruFin adapter names TRUSTAKE_CONTRACT_ADDR=0xcfab...006d on Ethereum; Etherscan V2 shows it is a TransparentUpgradeableProxy whose implementation is verified as ContractName=Staker. Both proxy and impl return bytecode. FOUND (proxy = live instance, impl = audited Staker code).

units.known_address_notes: Lavarage is a Solana spot-margin/lending Anchor program (Code4rena 2024-04). The deployed app bundle carries the program registry: programId '1avaAUcjccXCjSZzwUvB2gS3DzkkieV2Mw8CjdN65uu' (vanity prefix '1ava') with nodeWalletAddress 0x-style fee accounts, plus 'CRSeeBqjDnm3UPefJ9gxrtngTsnQRhEJiTA345Q83X3v'; both accounts are executable BPF upgradeable programs on Solana mainnet (verified via Alchemy solana-mainnet getAccountInfo). The SDK (pinedefi/lavarage-sdk) corroborates the idl/lavaragev2.t

units.titles: In transferVesting, the grantorVesting.releaseRate is calculated incorrectly, which leads to the sender being able to unlock more tokens than were initially locked. | transferVesting creates an incorrect vesting for new users when they purchase a vesting, because stepsClaimed is the same for all sales, allowing an attacker to prematurely unlock too many tokens
units.known_address_notes: Audited contract names (SecondSwap_Marketplace/_MarketplaceSetting/_StepVesting/_VestingDeployer) match verified Ethereum deployments found via Blockscout name search; several per-issuer Marketplace instances exist (0xe7a7, 0x65bF, 0x5d0C, 0xA020, 0x6a8c) - 0xe7a7 chosen as anchor. DefiLlama lists Ethereum/Avalanche/Solana TVL chains. C4 repo hardhat config only wires Sepolia testnet, so mainnet addresses came from on-chain lookup.
